item.title: Swift: Execute Code After a Specified Delay
item.description:
“Swift: Execute Code After a Specified Delay”

When developing applications in Swift, a common requirement is to execute a piece of code not immediately, but after a certain delay. This is essential for various functionalities like displaying timed messages, scheduling background tasks, or creating animations. Fortunately, Swift provides robust mechanisms for handling such delayed executions, primarily through Grand Central Dispatch (GCD) and the NSTimer class.

Utilizing Grand Central Dispatch (GCD) with asyncAfter

GCD’s asyncAfter method is a powerful and efficient way to schedule code execution on a dispatch queue after a specified time.
